about: Plain-language hints for the commonest Python errors (docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md). Each row: an error type and a pattern for its message as the board prints it (board) and as the simulator prints it (sim); the hint names the line and where to look. Patterns use JavaScript named groups (?<name>...). Setting: evn.python.errorHints.

rows.hint: Line {line}: look at how far in this line begins, and how far in the line above it begins.

board.pattern: ^unindent doesn't match any outer indent level$

sim.pattern: ^unindent does not match any outer indentation level$

rows.hint: Line {line}: look at how far in this line begins, and how far in each line above it begins.
Line {line}: look at this line and at the colon (:) that ends the line above it.

sim.pattern: ^(?:invalid syntax.*|expected ':'|'[(\[{]' was never closed|unmatched '[)\]}]'|closing parenthesis '[)\]}]' does not match opening parenthesis '[(\[{]'.*|unterminated (?:triple-quoted )?string literal.*|Missing parentheses in call to .*)$

rows.hint: Line {line}: look at this line and the one above it, sign by sign: colons, brackets, quote marks, and the spaces at the start.
Line {line}: look at '{name}' here and where it first appears above.
Line {line}: simtrail is a simulator-only module, for the panel's pen and errors; only the simulator has it.
Line {line}: look at the module name '{name}'; EVN's own module is called evn.
Line {line}: look at '{attr}' here; hover the name before the dot to see what it has.

board.pattern: ^\w+\(\) takes \d+ positional arguments but \d+ were given$

sim.pattern: ^\w+\(\) takes (?:from \d+ to )?\d+ positional arguments? but \d+ (?:was|were) given$

rows.hint: Line {line}: count the values in this call and the names in the def line of the function it calls.

board.pattern: ^function takes \d+ positional arguments but \d+ were given$

sim.pattern: ^\w+\.\w+\(\) takes (?:from \d+ to )?\d+ positional arguments? but \d+ (?:was|were) given$

rows.hint: Line {line}: count the values in the call on this line; hover the name to see what it takes.
Line {line}: look at the name '{kw}' before the = sign; hover the function to see the names it takes.

sim.pattern: ^'[^']+' not supported between instances of '[^']*' and '[^']*'$

rows.hint: Line {line}: look at the values on each side of the sign on this line.
Line {line}: look for round brackets ( ) after a name that holds a value, not a function.

sim.pattern: ^(?:(?:float |integer )?(?:division|modulo|floor division)(?: or modulo)? by zero|float divmod\(\)|float modulo|0\.0 cannot be raised to a negative power)$

rows.hint: Line {line}: look at the numbers on each side of /, //, %, ** or divmod on this line, and what each holds.
Line {line}: look at the number in [ ] and how many items there are; the first item is number 0.
Line {line}: look at each number given to a call on this line; the message above says which numbers it takes.

board.pattern: ^(?:\[Errno (?:5|19|110)\] (?:EIO|ENODEV|ETIMEDOUT)|16|.+ on port \d+ not responding|no .+ on port \d+ .*)$

sim.pattern: ^(?:the simulated robot has no .+|no .+ on port .+|\[Errno 110\] ETIMEDOUT)$

rows.hint: Line {line}: look at the device this line uses.
